question: to the Commission Bogdan Rzońca (ECR) Subject:

In the context of growing global economic competitiveness, changing regulatory frameworks and recent geopolitical events, the relocation of economic activity outside the EU may have significant consequences for the single market’s economic growth and competitiveness. I therefore ask the Commission to answer the following questions relating to the scale at which companies have been relocating from the European Union to third countries since 2020. I ask the Commission: 1.
How many companies have (fully or partially) relocated outside the EU since 2020?
What are the main destinations for relocation and which sectors are most affected by this phenomenon?
What are the main reasons behind this trend and its impact on the competitiveness of the EU economy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.6.2026) The European Restructuring Monitor (ERM)1 provides a repository of case studies and intelligence on restructuring trends. It has reported some 100 cases of offshoring to non-EU countries since 20202, primarily to India, China, the United States and Türkiye3. The observed trends are concentrated in the manufacturing industry, particularly electronics, textiles, transport equipment, machinery and chemicals, putting more than 30 000 jobs at risk4. The Commission closely monitors Europe’s competitiveness and analyses its underlying drivers, as presented in the 2026 Annual Single Market and Competitiveness Report5. The report underscores that barriers and administrative burden remain too high in the Single Market, including at national level. Moreover, high energy prices are weighing on industrial competitiveness and private investment momentum in the EU remains weak. Geopolitical tensions compound competitive pressures and expose vulnerabilities and strategic dependencies in Europe’s supply chains. To address these challenges, the Commission has adopted the Competitiveness Compass6 and subsequent initiatives such as the Clean Industrial Deal7, the Single Market Strategy8 and sectoral action plans9, alongside simplification packages10 to make business easier and faster in Europe. Together with the proposed Industrial Accelerator Act11, the 28th regime/’EU Inc.’12 and the forthcoming proposal for the Public Procurement Act, these measures will drive EU competitiveness and industrial renewal.

conditions on the size of the affected workforce are monitored in the ERM.
